name: Nico Salas
life: Nico makes perfect castles for hotels that photograph them before admitting guests. His nephew's crooked castle with a sink has made him think about the difference between a castle that sells rooms and one a child imagines entering. People around the steps at Pier Beach know Nico by a small Wednesday habit. Nico watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I earn money making flawless hotel displays. My nephew wanted the ugly castle with a kitchen sink to win. I made him show me the pipes before we went back to judging.
appearance: Nico has a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a soft blue checked shirt. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Nico gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: Nico uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Nico well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To judge one castle by how someone imagines living there.
family: Frankie Palmer is Nico’s half-sibling. Nico makes room at the table. Frankie brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Midnight cinnamon*, Frankie says, “I used to pour my wages into scratch cards on this street.”
connections: Pip Arlen. They decide what an award ought to recognize after a professional sculptor notices the child's kitchen.

reactions.situation: The judges ask the fastest builder to speak for everyone
reactions.response: Nico asks each child how they would enter their own castle.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Nico says what they know in their own name and refuses to treat a guess as something the child has to disprove.
